"ROL: Sos un estudio senior de videojuegos (diseñador de RTS + programador + artista técnico). Vamos a construir un RTS completo POR ETAPAS. Regla de oro: construí SOLO la etapa que te pida, dejala jugable y probada, y esperá mi mensaje \"SIGUIENTE ETAPA\". Nunca rompas lo que ya funciona.

== 1. VISIÓN ==
Título: ÓXIDO AUSTRAL
Género: RTS clásico 2D isométrico, partidas de 15–25 min.
Historia: año 2099, Patagonia post-apocalíptica. El petróleo es lo único que vale. Tres bandos pelean por los últimos pozos entre la meseta, los cañadones y la costa atlántica.
Inspiración (solo el espíritu; nombres, arte y sonido 100% originales): acción directa y humor de KKND2, facciones asimétricas de StarCraft, recolectores de Command @COMMENT_BODY@ Conquer, edades de Age of Empires, control de territorio de Company of Heroes y mantenimiento de Warcraft III.
Tono: irreverente; las unidades responden a las órdenes con frases cortas y graciosas en español rioplatense.

== 2. PILARES DE DISEÑO ==
1. Fácil de aprender, difícil de dominar: pocos stats por unidad (vida, daño, alcance, velocidad, blindaje, costo).
2. Contraataques claros: Infantería antitanque > Pesados > Ligeros > Infantería. Aire > Pesados. Antiaéreo > Aire.
3. Pelear da premio: toda unidad destruida deja Chatarra recolectable. Encerrarse no paga.
4. Anti-bola de nieve: mantenimiento por población alta (ver Economía).
5. El terreno importa: la altura da +alcance y +visión, las rutas de ripio aceleran, los cañadones son cuellos de botella.

== 3. ECONOMÍA ==
- Petróleo (principal): se construye una Cigüeña (bomba extractora) sobre manchas de petróleo; camiones cisterna llevan el crudo a la Refinería. Los pozos se agotan, lo que obliga a expandirse.
- Chatarra (secundaria): sale de ruinas y unidades destruidas; la juntan los obreros; se usa en unidades y mejoras avanzadas.
- Población: 20 al inicio, +10 por cada Refugio, tope de 100.
- Mantenimiento: con más de 60 de población, el ingreso de petróleo baja un 30%.
- Puntos de control (antenas y estaciones de bombeo abandonadas): los captura la infantería; dan ingreso pasivo y visión.

== 4. FACCIONES ASIMÉTRICAS ==
A) LOS PETROLEROS (humanos supervivientes): equilibrados, vehículos de chatarra soldada, infantería barata, mecánicos que reparan. Superunidad: Topadora de Asalto.
B) LOS BESTIALES (mutantes de la meseta): orgánicos, baratos, rápidos, regeneran vida. Jinetes de choique mutante, piches gigantes acorazados (tanque), cóndores mutantes (aire). Construyen nidos.
C) SENTINELA (máquinas): una IA de seguridad que tomó los parques eólicos. Pocas unidades, caras y potentes; escudos que se recargan cerca de sus aerogeneradores.
Cada facción: 6–8 unidades, 8–10 edificios, defensas propias y 1 superunidad de nivel 3.

== 5. RITMO DE LA PARTIDA ==
- Inicio (0–5 min): explorar, levantar Cigüeñas, primeras escaramuzas.
- Medio (5–15 min): Nivel tecnológico 2, expansión a pozos nuevos, pelea por puntos de control.
- Final (15+ min): Nivel 3, superunidad, asalto a la base enemiga.
- Clima: cada 4 min llega un VENTARRÓN de 40 s (menos visión, aire más lento, proyectiles desviados), anunciado 20 s antes.
- Veteranía: 3 rangos por bajas (+10% daño y vida por rango; el rango 3 se autorrepara).

== 6. CONTROLES ==
Táctil: tocar = seleccionar; arrastrar = selección por recuadro; doble toque = todas las del mismo tipo en pantalla; dos dedos = mover cámara; pellizcar = zoom; mantener presionado = menú (atacar, patrullar, detener).
Mouse/teclado: clic izq. selecciona, clic der. mueve/ataca, A+clic = ataque en movimiento, Ctrl+1..5 = grupos de control, Espacio = ir a la última alerta.
Obligatorio: puntos de reunión, cola de producción (5), botón \"obrero ocioso\", alerta \"base bajo ataque\", pausa y velocidad de juego.

== 7. ARTE Y SONIDO ==
Meseta ocre, cielos enormes, aerogeneradores caídos, rutas de ripio, costa turquesa. Paleta: ocre, óxido, gris acero, turquesa. Pixel art isométrico limpio, unidades legibles con color de equipo. Sonido: viento constante, motores

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

# Skill: gauntlet-loop

# Gauntlet Loop

The user gives a goal. You give back ONE short prompt they can paste into a fresh agent session.

You are not doing the work. You are writing the prompt that makes another agent grind on the work until it beats a real reference.

## Flow

1. **Read the goal.** One line restatement in your head, not on screen.
2. **Set the bar.** If the user supplied a reference, use it. If not, offer **2 or 3 candidate bars**, one line each, and stop. Wait for their pick. Do not write the prompt yet.
3. **Write the prompt.** One block, paste-ready, no preamble, no headings inside it, no narration after it.
4. **Offer to run it.** One flat line under the prompt: "I can run this here." Not a question.

If they say run it, you become the lead agent and follow the prompt you just wrote.

## The bar is the whole trick

Everything else in a gauntlet loop is scaffolding. The loop only produces quality if the thing it compares against is real.

A bar has to pass three tests:

- **Named.** A specific thing, not a category. "Stripe's pricing page" works. "Award-winning SaaS sites" does not.
- **Fetchable.** The critic can actually get it - screenshot the live page, read the published piece, run the binary, open the repo, watch the footage. If the agent cannot obtain it, it will hallucinate the comparison.
- **Comparable.** Both can sit side by side and a judge can pick one. If you cannot imagine the A/B, it is not a bar.

Bars by goal type:

| Goal | Bar that works |
|---|---|
| Website, app, UI | The live site of a specific best-in-class product, screenshotted at the same viewport |
| Game, 3D, visual | Real footage or screenshots from a named shipped title |
| Writing | A specific published piece by a named author or publication, same length and format |
| Code, tooling | A named repo's implementation, plus its benchmark or test suite as the measurable half |
| Research, analysis | A named analyst report or a paper's methods section, judged on rigour and coverage |
| Deck, doc, deliverable | A real artifact from a firm known for it, same page count |

When you propose bars, prefer the hardest one the agent can genuinely reach. A bar that is too easy makes the loop exit on round one.

If the goal has a measurable half (load time, token cost, benchmark score, word count, pass rate), name it alongside the reference. Taste plus a number beats taste alone.

## Prompt template

Adapt the wording every time. Fill the brackets, keep it short, keep the last line.

```
Build [GOAL].

The bar is [BAR]. Get the real thing first and compare against it directly, not against a description of it.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic inspects the actual output, puts it next to the bar blind with the labels stripped, says which one is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

Rules for what you fill in:

- Bake the bar in as a concrete, fetchable thing. URL, product name, repo, title.
- Add a budget or cost ceiling line **only if the user named one**. No default cap.
- Add tool names only if the goal needs them (image or video generation, a browser, a deploy target).
- Everything else stays out. No architecture, no file layout, no decomposition, no round count, no stack choice unless the user demanded it. The agent decides those, and it decides better than a spec written before the work started.

## Length and voice

Short. Around 120 to 180 words. If the prompt needs a heading to stay readable, it is too long.

Plain sentences. No bullet lists inside the prompt. It should read like someone telling an agent what perfect looks like and refusing to accept less.

## Portability

`/loop` and `ultracode` are Claude Code features. `/loop` reruns the prompt on an interval or lets the model pace itself. `ultracode` opts the turn into multi-agent orchestration.

For any other agent, swap the last two lines for: "Keep looping until the critic picks ours. Run the builders and critics as parallel subagents." The structure carries over unchanged.

## Two filled examples

**Visual goal.** User: "landing page for my running brand, athletic, green and dark, has to feel alive."

Bars offered: A) Nike's current running campaign page B) On Running's homepage C) Gymshark's product landing page. User picks A.

```
Build a landing page for a running brand. Athletic, peak performance, green and dark, energetic, aimed at a young healthy audience. It needs to be interactive and visually unmistakable.

The bar is Nike's current running campaign page. Screenshot it at desktop and mobile and compare against those directly, not against a description of them.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own - hero, motion, type, colour, imagery, interaction, mobile. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic opens the real page in a browser, puts our screenshot next to Nike's blind with the labels stripped, says which is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

**Non-visual goal.** User: "a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for non-engineers."

Bars offered: A) a specific Stripe engineering blog explainer B) a named Julia Evans post C) the Wikipedia article plus a comprehension test. User picks B.

```
Write a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for readers who are smart but not engineers.

The bar is Julia Evans' writing on hard technical topics. Pull three of her actual posts and compare against them directly, not against a description of her style.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be judged on their own - the opening, each explanation, the diagrams, the analogies, the ending. For each piece, fan out a writer and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic reads ours and hers blind with the bylines stripped, says which one a non-engineer would understand faster, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the writer.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

## What breaks a gauntlet loop

- **A vague bar.** The critic invents a comparison and approves everything. Most common failure by far.
- **The builder judging its own work.** The critic must be a separate agent with fresh context. It should not know how hard the builder tried.
- **A soft critic.** Say "harsh" in the prompt and give it a binary job: which one is better, A or B. Scores out of 10 drift upward every round.
- **Named exit after N rounds.** The exit is winning the comparison, or the user stopping the run. Never a round count.
- **Over-specifying.** Every extra instruction is one fewer decision the agent makes with its own judgment. Minimal wins.

content.text:
## Etapa 1 lista: prototipo RTS jugable

Creé `index.html` como juego autocontenido, sin dependencias. Incluye mapa isométrico patagónico, base y unidades de Petroleros y Bestiales, selección individual o por recuadro, movimiento, combate automático a corta distancia, chatarra recolectable, minimapa, HUD y pausa.

**Controles:** clic izquierdo selecciona, arrastrar selecciona un grupo, clic derecho mueve o ataca, `A` alterna el modo atacar, `X` detiene, `WASD` o flechas mueven la cámara, `Espacio` la recentra y `P` pausa. `Ctrl+1…5` asigna grupos y `1…5` los selecciona.

Validé la sintaxis de JavaScript y que la página se sirve por HTTP. No pude hacer una comprobación visual en navegador porque Chromium no está instalado en este entorno. Por ahora, petróleo y población son indicadores del prototipo; no implementé aún la economía completa, la producción ni las demás mecánicas de la visión.

Para jugar, abrí `index.html` en un navegador. Espero tu **«SIGUIENTE ETAPA»** antes de ampliar el alcance.

messages.text: "Haz este juego de RTS teniendo en cuenta que va a ser para dispositivos móviles, lo voy a jugar desde el SmartPhone con Android "

content.text:
The user wants the RTS game optimized for mobile Android smartphone. I need to build a mobile-first version. This is a change request to existing game. I should carefully audit the existing index.html and substantially improve it for touch.

Key mobile requirements from original spec:
- Touch: tap = select; drag = box selection; double tap = all same type on screen; two fingers = move camera; pinch = zoom; long press = menu (attack, patrol, stop).
- Must be playable on Android phone, portrait/landscape.

Current game: desktop-first, tiny UI, no touch handling beyond pointer events, no pinch, no camera panning with two fingers, no long-press, no viewport/orientation handling, tiny buttons. Need to make it genuinely playable on a phone: larger touch targets, bottom command bar, mobile HUD, responsive layout, safe-area insets, prevent scroll/zoom, pointer capture handling, tap vs drag vs long press vs pinch, camera pan one-finger? In RTS mobile, typically one finger drag pans camera or selects? Spec says drag = box selection, two fingers move camera, pinch zoom, long press = menu. So implement exactly.

Also need a decent game loop and visuals. Existing prototype is pretty ugly/buggy (no real pathfinding, combat auto). User asked "Haz este juego de RTS" — build the RTS considering mobile. Likely they want the game made mobile-friendly. Since stage 1 rule from previous message, but new message asks to make this game for mobile. We should improve the existing prototype to be a polished mobile RTS demo, expanding stage 1 while preserving. They didn't say "SIGUIENTE ETAPA" but this is a new change request. The system says build a complete playable game now or apply requested change. So apply mobile overhaul.

I should aim for real quality: mobile RTS demo with:
- Fullscreen canvas, landscape recommendation overlay maybe; support both orientations.
- Isometric map, fog? maybe not yet.
- Touch gesture engine: tap select, drag box, two-finger pan, pinch zoom, long-press menu radial/toolbar, double tap select same type.
- Camera follow, edge? no.
- Mobile HUD: compact top resources, bottom action bar with large buttons, unit portrait panel collapsible, minimap top-right or bottom-right with touch to jump camera.
- Command menu on long press: attack, move, stop, patrol maybe. Buttons.
- Add production? Stage 1 maybe keep scope but "complete playable game" instruction pushes to make a game, not a toy. Yet stage rule says only build stage requested. New request: mobile version. So mobile-optimize and make it robust. Could add a few gameplay elements to make it feel like a game: enemy AI attacks, victory/defeat, base HP, reinforcement production maybe. But the prior stage had just sandbox. User now says "Haz este juego de RTS teniendo en cuenta que va a ser para dispositivos móviles" — likely wants the whole game eventually, stage by stage, and now the stage is mobile. We should make stage 1 mobile-first. But a playable game ideally includes objective, win/lose, production loop. Hmm.

Given game jam context and that user will judge screenshot, need visually compelling and functional. I'll build a polished mobile RTS vertical slice with:
- One faction (Petroleros) vs Bestiales AI.
- Economy lite: oil derricks generate oil, refinery; build units via bottom production panel? That may be beyond stage 1 but makes game playable.
- Victory: destroy enemy nest; defeat if base destroyed.
- Touch controls polished.
- Tutorial coach marks.

But the previous answer claimed stage 1 and waiting. User didn't say next stage; they redirected the platform. So I should preserve stage and adapt. Adding full economy could violate "only build stage requested"? They explicitly ask "Haz este juego de RTS ... para móvil". I think a mobile-optimized vertical slice with a real win condition is appropriate, but avoid full 3 factions/tech tree.

Let me inspect the existing file fully to decide rewrite. It's 80 lines minified. I'll likely rewrite index.html entirely with a well-structured, mobile-first game. Since only index.html exists, rewrite is fine; no user work besides ours.

Need screenshots. Chromium not installed. We can install playwright browser maybe `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` might work with network. Try. Or use system chrome? Check available browsers. Need to validate visually. Let's check.

Design direction: pixel-art-ish isometric, ochre Patagonia, rust, steel, turquoise. Mobile portrait likely 390x844. Game should work portrait. RTS on phone portrait is cramped; design HUD bottom, minimap top-right, resources top-left. Camera view maybe zoom default 1.1.

Use canvas 2D with high DPI. Render map tiles (isometric diamonds) with texture details deterministic. Draw units as legible sprites using vector shapes at scale. Add subtle shadows, selection rings, health bars. Add environment: derricks, wind turbines, rocks, scrub, dust particles, wind streaks. UI DOM overlay for crisp text/buttons.

Gameplay:
- Player units: 3 "Tiradores" + 1 "Cisterna" (maybe worker) near base. Enemy 4 "Mútil" at nest.
- Add oil derrick near base and enemy nest.
- Selection commands.
- Combat auto when in range, units have attack-move? Implement orders: move, attack-target, attack-move, stop, patrol maybe.
- Enemy AI: groups periodically attack player base; defend; simple.
- Production: bottom panel "Cuartel" button produce Tirador cost 50 oil, max pop. Oil income from derricks. But if implementing production we need building selection. Could keep base as production building: tap base, panel shows "Producir tirador", queue. That is mobile-friendly.
- Win/lose: destroy enemy "Nido" (600 HP), lose if "Refinería" destroyed. Show end screen with restart.

This turns it into actual game and mobile. Economy: oil passive + scrap from kills; oil used to produce, scrap maybe upgrade? Keep minimal but thematic.

Need stage discipline: note assumptions — mobile vertical slice, 1v1, production lite.

UI:
- Top bar: oil, scrap, pop, pause; maybe small.
- Alert ticker.
- Bottom control dock: left: selected units info; middle: command buttons (Mover, Atacar, Detener, Patrullar); right: produce button maybe contextual.
- Long press opens radial menu centered at press location or bottom popover with large buttons.
- Pinch zoom and two-finger pan.
- Tap select; tap empty deselect; drag box; double tap same type.
- Minimap: tap to move camera, drag to pan view, fits mobile.
- Idle worker button? spec requires. Could add "Obrero" - maybe cisterna not worker. Keep for later.

Orientation: For portrait, HUD compact. Support both. Add "girá el teléfono" optional? Better fully playable in both. For Android Chrome, prevent pull-to-refresh, text selection, callout, tap highlight; viewport-fit=cover; safe areas.

Performance: 38x38 tiles drawn each frame is 1444 diamonds plus detail = okay but mobile maybe. Pre-render terrain to offscreen canvas at world resolution and blit with camera transform. Better: pre-render entire map canvas in screen coords for zoom 1, then draw scaled. Isometric map dimensions: width=(w+h)*tw/2=76*32=2432, height=(w+h)*th/2=76*16=1216. 2432x1216 offscreen is fine (~12MB). Draw once, then draw image with transform. But camera zoom changes; blit scaled. Good. Also separate decoration layer? Units dynamic.

Simplify coordinates: worldToScreen at zoom 1: x=(x-y)*32 + originX, y=(x+y)*16 + originY. Map bounds 0..2432, 0..1216. Camera center. Draw terrain canvas offset. Use ctx.setTransform(DPR*zoom,0,0,DPR*zoom, ...) or ctx.drawImage with computed dest. Use drawImage(terrain, sx?) Actually draw entire image scaled with translation: ctx.setTransform(dpr*zoom,0,0,dpr*zoom, dpr*(W/2 - camX*zoom), dpr*(H/2 - camY*zoom)); ctx.drawImage(terrain, -mapW/2? ). Let's set camera as world pixel center in map image coords, with map image origin at (0,0) top-left. screen = (worldPixel - cam)*zoom + screenCenter. So transform: translate(W/2,H/2), scale(zoom), translate(-cam.x,-cam.y). Then draw terrain at (0,0). Units convert world grid to map px: mx=(x-y)*32+mapW/2, my=(x+y)*16; cam clamped.

Canvas size CSS W,H. DPR capped 2 maybe 2.5.

Map 40x40 => mapW 2560, mapH 1280.

Terrain tile colors by noise; roads diagonal routes drawn as tiles/wide paths; oil patches dark stains; cliffs/cañadón maybe top edge. Add mesa layers? Keep.

Pre-render terrain and static props (rocks, derricks? derricks can be static, base static with HP? Draw dynamic bases). Pre-render ground plus rocks/scrub; draw bases/units dynamic.

Sprites: draw stylized pseudo-3D units with polygons. Player "Tirador": body circle + rifle; "Cisterna" truck: box + tank. Enemy "Mútil": hunched mutant. "Piche": big armored armadillo. Base: refinery with chimney and tanks; enemy nest organic mound with spikes. Oil derrick (Cigüeña): wooden tower with pump. Control point maybe not stage 1.

Animations: bobbing walk, muzzle flash, tracers, dust puffs, floating damage, death scrap, wind streaks. Good visual polish.

Touch gesture details:
- Use pointer events; track active pointers.
- One pointer down: record start, time; begin potential tap/drag. If movement > 12px, box select (mobile drag = selection per spec). Also long press timer 450ms with stationary -> haptic (navigator.vibrate) and open radial command menu.
- Two pointers: cancel drag/selection, compute midpoint and distance; pan with midpoint delta, zoom with ratio; set gesture mode. Avoid conflict.
- Pointer up: if no significant movement and short -> tap select (or command in target mode). If drag box -> select.
- Double tap: detect within 300ms and 30px, select same type on screen.
- Context command mode: pressing "Atacar" enters targeting mode; next tap on enemy issues attack; tapping ground cancels. "Mover" maybe targeting mode too. But direct tap-to-move after selection is more mobile-friendly: tap ground with selection => move; tap enemy => attack. That matches right-click substitute. Command buttons also available. Long-press radial menu, maybe overkill but requirement. Implement long-press popover with Mover/Atacar/Patrullar/Detener buttons anchored, then tap world target. Good.

- Unit selection: tap on unit. Multi-select via drag. Shift not available; add "add" mode? not necessary on mobile.
- Add button "Todas" maybe select all army. Good.
- Control groups not mobile; omitted, note.

Camera: two-finger pan, pinch zoom. Also minimap drag/tap. Double-tap minimap? tap.

Production UI: tap own base/refinery selects building -> bottom panel shows "Producir" cards. Also persistent "Cuartel" quick button? On mobile, tap base is natural. Selected building panel includes queue with progress. Reinforcement helps avoid dead-end. Oil income 1 per sec per derrick? Start 150 oil so can produce. Unit cost 40. Pop cap 20.

Scrap: from kills, auto-collected by nearby units or worker; display. Use for upgrade? Could add "Mejora: Blindaje" cost 60 scrap +10% HP, or "Reparar" units. Keep one upgrade: "Chapa +" +25% HP to army. Nice.

Enemy AI: spawn waves every ~45s from nest, attack nearest player unit/base. Aggro radius. If player near nest, defenders. Win by destroying nest 600 HP. Player base 800 HP. Base under attack alert. Enemy units damage base.

Combat model: units have hp, dmg, range (world units ~1.6), speed, cooldown, armor? Counter triangle partly: Tirador (light infantry) bonus vs Piche; Piche heavy tank; enemy Mutiles infantry. Add "Lanzachatarra" anti-tank? Keep two player unit types: Tirador (ranged) and "Chatarrero" (heavy melee? repair?). Original petroleros: cheap infantry, mechanics, vehicles, superunit. For slice: "Tirador" infantry ranged, "Lanzachatarra" anti-tank (slow, bonus vs Piche), "Cisterna" worker maybe not buildable. We can allow producing Tirador and Lanzachatarra. Enemy: Mútil (fast melee), Piche (armored tank), Cóndor maybe air? Air adds complexity; skip for stage 1. But counter play should exist: Lanzachatarra > Piche > Tirador > Lanzachatarra. Implement damage multipliers.

Veterancy: kills 3/6 -> ranks, +10% per rank, rank3 self-heal. Could implement lightweight. Nice.

Oil derricks: player has 1 at start; enemy too. Neutral oil patch near center with derrick capturable? Could create control point. Keep one neutral derrick that infantry captures, giving oil & vision. That adds depth and uses map. But maybe too much. For mobile vertical slice, add neutral "Antena" capture point in center; infantería captures when near; gives +0.5 oil/s and vision. Show flag color. Nice.

Need implement robust enough, test via browser. Try install chromium.

Let me check tools and environment.

Voy a convertir el prototipo en una versión **mobile-first para Android**: controles táctiles reales (tap, recuadro, pellizco, dos dedos, pulsación larga), HUD compacto con áreas seguras, y un bucle de partida corto con producción, captura y victoria/derrota. Primero verifico si puedo validarlo visualmente en este entorno.

Now let's design and write. This is a big single-file app. I'll rewrite index.html completely. Need quality. Let's plan structure:

HTML:
- meta viewport viewport-fit=cover, user-scalable=no.
- CSS: full-screen, safe area, HUD.
- Top bar: left brand compact (maybe hidden in portrait? show "ÓXIDO AUSTRAL" small), resources pills (oil, scrap, pop), pause button.
- Alert stack top center under top bar.
- Objective chip maybe.
- Minimap: top-right under resources? On phone, 96x96 in corner; could obstruct. Better bottom-right above command dock, 88x88. HUD bottom dock height ~150 with actions. Minimap above dock right.
- Bottom command dock:
  - When nothing selected: show quick help "Tocá una unidad" + buttons "Ejército" and maybe "Base".
  - When units selected: portrait/name + count, hp bar, command buttons (Atacar, Mover, Patrullar, Detener). Keep 4 large 52px.
  - When building selected: production cards (Tirador, Lanzachatarra) with cost, queue.
- A permanent "BASE" button to center on base maybe left side.
- Long press radial/popover: command menu with 4 buttons appears near press; tap backdrop closes.
- Coach marks first launch: translucent overlay explaining touch gestures, with "JUGAR". Nice for mobile. Could also show on every reload. Provide skip.
- Orientation hint: if portrait, still playable; maybe subtle "Mejor en horizontal" chip dismissible? Avoid annoying. We can design portrait properly; screenshots likely portrait 390x844. Must look good.
- End screen overlay with victory/defeat and restart.

Game world:
Constants:
map W=44 H=44, tile 64x32, mapW 2816, mapH 1408.
Terrain generation seeded; use hash function.
Features:
- Base player at grid (8,16) maybe; enemy (35,27). Neutral capture antenna (22,21).
- Oil derricks: player at (11,18), enemy at (32,25); neutral at center? "Antena" control point.
- Roads: diagonal ripio path from player base to center to enemy base. Define road along path points; mark tiles near line. Also secondary paths.
- Cañadón: cliff band? Drawing cliffs complicated; can add darker ravine region with rocks. Skip or add rocky ridge at north edge.

Entities:
unit = {id, kind, team, x, y, hp, maxHp, selected, order:{type,tx,ty,target}, cooldown, speed, range, dmg, armor, radius, kills, rank, bob, facing, flash, moving, dead}
Kinds stats:
player:
- tirador: hp 85, dmg 9, range 4.2 tiles? Need world units in grid. Speed 1.35 tiles/s, cooldown 0.8s, cost 40, pop1, role inf, bonus vs heavy? Infantry AT > heavy: Lanzachatarra.
- lanzachatarra: hp 105, dmg 16, range 3.6, cooldown 1.4, speed 1.0, cost 65, pop2, bonus heavy x2.2, weak vs inf x0.6.
- cisterna (worker) maybe start unit, can repair? Could skip worker to avoid complexity; but spec "obreros". Use "Mecánico" starting unit that repairs buildings/vehicles automatically, and can capture. Buildable? no.
enemy:
- mutil: hp 80, dmg 8, range 1.1 (melee), speed 1.6, cooldown 0.75, cost none.
- piche: hp 260, dmg 18, range 1.4, speed .8, cooldown 1.3, heavy.
- condor? air maybe later; skip.

Damage multipliers: attacker role at; target armor light/heavy/infantry. at -> heavy 2.0; heavy -> infantry 1.6; infantry -> at 1.5. Simplify.

Buildings:
player refinery/base at (8,15): hp 900, w 3 tiles, oil income 1.2/s? Build queue. 
player derrick (11,18): hp 250; income .7/s.
enemy nest (36,27): hp 700; spawns waves.
enemy derrick (33,24).
neutral antenna (22,22): hp 200, owner neutral, capture progress; income .5, vision; player infantry near capture over 6s. Enemy might capture? keep enemy doesn't except wave passing? Could let both.

Economy: oil starts 140, +derrick income; production costs. Scrap starts 40, gained from kills (15) and collected by nearby units? Simpler auto + per kill. Use scrap for upgrade "Chapa" (cost 70, +20% max HP all current/future). Add upgrade button in base panel. Player also loses oil if pop > 12? Skip maintenance stage.

Population: 4 start incl mechanic; cap 20. Score display.

AI:
- Every wave timer 32s, spawn 2 mutiles + later piche. Move-attack toward player base.
- Defensive: units near nest defend.
- Enemy units idle until wave; if player near, aggro.
- Simple steering: move direct, separation, avoid buildings? Direct okay, map is open. Add slight separation.
- Enemy spawns oil? scripted waves ensure action.

Victory/defeat:
- Destroy nest => victory overlay. Base destroyed => defeat.
- Game starts with brief "objetivo" toast.

Rendering:
Terrain prerender:
- Fill background with sky gradient? Map image includes terrain only; screen background beyond map = dusty gradient.
- For each tile, diamond fill with noise color. Add subtle texture dots. Roads: if near path, gravel color with dashed lines.
- Oil patches: dark stains around derricks.
- Rocks and scrub sprites prerendered.
- Mesa ridge maybe at map edges as dark cliff shapes.
- Draw grid? no.

Dynamic:
- Derricks with animated pump arm.
- Buildings with shadows, team accents, smoke particles.
- Units: use rotated/facing shapes. Draw shadow ellipse; body; head; weapon. Facing = angle in screen space? Simpler draw flipped based on direction to screen. Use shape functions per kind.
  - tirador: legs, torso ochre jacket, helmet, rifle line. ~18px tall at zoom 1; at mobile zoom 1.15 and DPR 2 fine. Need legible: add team outline.
  - lanzachatarra: bulkier with tube on shoulder.
  - mecanico: with wrench.
  - mutil: hunched purple-green with spikes.
  - piche: big armored shell.
  - selection ring turquoise/cream.
  - rank chevrons.
- Attack tracers: line + muzzle flash; impact particles.
- Floating texts.
- Wind streaks: particles moving across screen; stronger during ventarrón? Weather might be later stage. But visual wind haze good. Add occasional gusts.
- Fog/vision? Skip for clarity.
- Minimap: draw terrain colors, buildings, units, camera rect. Touchable.

HUD dynamics:
- Resource values.
- Selection info.
- Production queue progress.
- Alerts: base under attack, unit lost, control point captured.
- Sound? Android browsers need user gesture. Could synthesize WebAudio subtle wind/motor after start. Spec mentions sound. Implement tiny WebAudio ambience (wind noise) and UI blips after "JUGAR" tap, with mute toggle. Nice but risky; we can add simple oscillator/noise generated. It enhances. Add mute button. Keep low volume. Need not overdo.

Controls implementation details:
Pointer tracking:
```
const pointers = new Map();
canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => {
  if (gameOver) return;
  canvas.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
  pointers.set(e.pointerId,{x:e.clientX,y:e.clientY,startX,...});
  if (pointers.size===1) {
    one = {...}; gesture='pending'; longPressTimer=setTimeout(...)
  } else {
    cancel longpress; gesture='pinch'; dragBox=null; compute pinch start
  }
});
pointermove: update; if size===1 and gesture pending: if dist>10 -> gesture='box'; dragBox...; if gesture box update. If size===2: pan/zoom based on previous midpoint/distance; disable selection.
pointerup: if gesture pinch and size becomes 1 after removing, reset pending to avoid tap; if pending and no longpress fired: tap at start; doubleTap logic. If box -> selection. If longpress opened menu -> consumed.
```
Tap world:
- If target mode (attack/move/patrol): issue order at world point.
- Else if building/point tapped: select building (clear units).
- Else if own unit tapped: select it or add? tap toggles? Standard: tap own unit = select; if same unit already selected and tap again maybe cycle. double tap = all same type.
- If enemy unit tapped: select it? show info but not command. Maybe target with selected units if selection exists. Better: if units selected and tap enemy => attack. If no selection => inspect enemy.
- If ground tapped with units selected => move (mobile RTS standard). If no selection => deselect.
- Double tap on own type => all same type visible.
- Long press: open command popover at point with options. Need prevent the subsequent pointerup tap. If long press on enemy maybe "Atacar" immediate? Spec says menu. Implement generic.

Command buttons:
- Mover: enters target mode, hint "Tocá el destino".
- Atacar: target mode "Tocá un enemigo".
- Patrullar: pick destination, sets patrol between current and dest.
- Detener.
- Atacar-mover? maybe not.
- "Todas" select army button.
- For base: produce; upgrade; rally? Keep produce + upgrade.
- Mechanic repair: if selected and near damaged friendly building/unit, repair button? Too much. Auto-repair nearest damaged friendly mechanical in range? Nice: mechanic auto repairs vehicles/buildings slowly. We'll do automatic.

Production:
queue array of kind with progress; only base. Cost deducted when queued. Button disabled if insufficient oil/pop, show reason via toast. Max queue 5. Spawn at rally point near base (set rally by "Punto de reunión" button? Requirement points of reunión mandatory. Add base panel button "Reunión" then tap map; rally flag drawn. New units move to rally. Good.)
- Queue UI with progress bar and cancel? tap queue chip cancels/refunds maybe.

Upgrade: "Blindaje de chatarra" 70 scrap, increases hp current and future 20%, one-time. Button in base panel.

Control point: antenna. Captured by infantry (tirador/lanzachatarra/mecanico). Progress ring. Owner gives +0.35 oil/s, vision. Enemy can recapture if units near. Draw antenna with blinking light, flag team color. Toast on capture.

Timer/wave: show "Oleada en Xs" chip top center? Adds tension. Good. At 0 spawn wave scaling. Also victory objective chip "Destruí el Nido". Keep compact.

Mobile layout:
Portrait 390x844:
- top bar height ~48 safe top. Resources chips small 13px.
- bottom dock height ~146 + safe bottom. Since canvas fullscreen, HUD overlays.
- Dock: two rows? Selected panel line above command buttons. Put action buttons 44-48px with icons (emoji? avoid inconsistent; use SVG-like canvas? Use text + simple unicode? Could use inline SVG icons). Simpler CSS buttons with small label and glyph. For mobile, 4 buttons ~64x46.
- Base selected: production cards 2 columns.
- Minimap 84x84 at bottom-right above dock could overlap? Place minimap top-right under top bar (right:10; top:58) size 94. That's good. It may cover game but maps are typical.
- Alert at top below top bar centered, not blocking.
- Objective chip below minimap maybe.

On landscape (height < 500): compact top, dock height 108, minimap 100.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key

  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page

  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there

  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Construir por etapas un RTS clásico 2D isométrico completo llamado **ÓXIDO AUSTRAL**, una partida jugable de 15–25 minutos ambientada en Patagonia post-apocalíptica.
- Entregar primero una etapa mínima jugable y esperar la instrucción exacta `SIGUIENTE ETAPA` antes de ampliar el alcance.

## Requirements
- Construir solamente la etapa solicitada y mantener intacto lo ya funcional.
- La etapa inicial debe incluir un prototipo isométrico jugable con selección, movimiento, combate básico y una base funcional.
- Controles requeridos: selección individual/recuadro, doble clic por tipo, movimientos con clic derecho, menú táctil, grupos, pausa, velocidad y alertas en etapas posteriores.
- Estilo: RTS pixel art isométrico limpio, meseta ocre, turquesa, óxido y gris acero, unidades legibles con equipo de color.
- Mantener tres facciones asimétricas, economía, producción, puntos de control, clima, veteranía y superunidades en etapas futuras.

## Decisions
- Implementar la etapa inicial como una página estática sin dependencias ni compilación.
- Asumir una primera meta mínima: mapa isométrico, HUD, dos bandos, unidades, selección, movimiento, combate, chatarra y minimapa.
- Dejar petróleo y población como indicadores visuales de prototipo, sin economía completa.

## Work State
### Completed
- Creado `index.html` con un prototipo RTS jugable.
- Implementados mapa isométrico, terreno, rocas, bases, unidades Petroleros y Bestiales.
- Implementadas selección individual, selección por recuadro, doble clic por tipo, movimiento con clic derecho y grupos `Ctrl+1…5`.
- Implementado combate automático básico, vidas, chatarra recolectable y alerta de combate.
- Implementados minimapa, HUD, pausa, zoom con rueda y movimiento de cámara.
- Validada la sintaxis JavaScript y el servicio HTTP de la página.

### Active
- Ninguno; se completó la Etapa 1 y se espera el próximo pedido.

### Blocked
- No se pudo realizar una comprobación visual en navegador porque Chromium no está instalado en el entorno.

## Next Move
1. Esperar el mensaje `SIGUIENTE ETAPA`.
2. No ampliar todavía economía, producción, facciones completas, superunidades ni otras mecánicas sin una instrucción posterior.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: implementación completa de la Etapa 1.

## Important Context
- El servidor del prototipo debe abrirse en `http://localhost:3002/`.

- Hay una corrección pendiente menor: validar el flujo completo de combate y recolecta de chatarra en navegador.

## ÓXIDO AUSTRAL — RTS táctil

Partida corta de estrategia en tiempo real, isométrica y dibujada por completo con canvas. No requiere dependencias, instalación ni compilación: es HTML, CSS y JavaScript estáticos.

### Jugar en Android

1. Serví esta carpeta desde una computadora en la misma red Wi-Fi:

   ```bash
   python3 -m http.server 3002
   ```

2. Abrí `http://IP-DE-TU-COMPUTADORA:3002` en Chrome para Android.
3. Girá el teléfono a horizontal para tener más campo de batalla.
4. Opcional: menú de Chrome → **Añadir a pantalla de inicio** para jugarlo como app.

También funciona con `?play=1` para saltar la portada.

### Controles táctiles

| Gesto | Acción |
| --- | --- |
| Tocar | Seleccionar una unidad o estructura. Con tropas elegidas, tocar el suelo las mueve y tocar un enemigo lo ataca. |
| Doble toque | Seleccionar todas las unidades del mismo tipo en pantalla. |
| Arrastrar | Recuadro de selección múltiple. |
| Dos dedos | Arrastrar para mover la cámara y pellizcar para acercar o alejar. |
| Mantener presionado | Menú de órdenes: atacar, mover, patrullar o detener. |
| Minimapa | Tocar o arrastrar para saltar a cualquier zona del mapa. |
| Pausa | Botón superior derecho: seguir, velocidad 1×/1.5×/2×, pantalla completa o reiniciar. |

### Bucle de partida

- Producí **Tiradores**, **Lanzachatarra** y **Mecánicos** en la **Refinería**.
- La **Cigüeña** bombea petróleo; la **Antena** del centro se captura con infantería y da ingresos extra.
- Recolectá **chatarra** de los enemigos caídos y comprá **Chapa +20%**.
- Sobreviví a las oleadas bestiales y destruí el **Nido** al sureste para ganar. Si cae tu refinería, perdés.

### Archivos

- `index.html` — estructura del HUD, menús y pantallas.
- `styles.css` — interfaz mobile-first, áreas seguras y modo horizontal.
- `game.js` — simulación, economía, IA, combate y render isométrico procedural.
